title: Artificial selection

draft.title: Artificial selection
card: In artificial selection, people choose which plants or animals breed. They pick individuals with traits they want, such as a calm nature or large grains.
Individuals in a population vary, and some of this variation is inherited. Offspring of the chosen parents are more likely to have the wanted trait.
If this choice is repeated over many generations, the wanted trait becomes more common in the population. Dog breeds and high-yield wheat were produced this way.
The process is the same as natural selection, except that people, not the environment, decide which individuals breed.
draft.remember: In artificial selection, people choose the parents, and the chosen traits become more common over generations.

a.q: A farmer in Western Australia sows only seed from her highest-yielding wheat plants each year. What is she doing?
opts: Choosing which plants breed to make a wanted trait common
Causing wheat plants to mutate so that they grow more grain
Letting the environment decide which wheat plants survive
Changing the traits of each plant by giving it better care
a.why: She picks which plants breed, so high yield becomes more common over generations. Better care would not change the seed's inherited traits, and here the farmer, not the environment, decides which plants breed.
a.clue: Who decides which plants pass on their seed?

b.q: Wool from some of Tomas's sheep in Tasmania is finer than the rest. He breeds only from those sheep for many years. What is the likely result?
opts: Fine wool becomes more common in his flock
Each sheep grows finer wool as it ages
Fine wool becomes less common in his flock
His flock stops varying in any trait at all
b.why: Only sheep with fine wool breed, and the trait is inherited, so more lambs have it and it becomes more common. A sheep does not change its own traits to suit the breeder, and variation in other traits can remain.
b.clue: Think about which sheep have lambs, and what lambs inherit.

a.best: Choosing which plants breed to make a wanted trait common

b.best: Fine wool becomes more common in his flock
